newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-INDIA LEVELS DAVIS CUP TIE WITH CZECHS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-INDIA LEVELS DAVIS CUP TIE WITH CZECHS.

text.p: Leander Paes upset Jiri Novak to bring underdog India level with the Czech Republic after the opening singles matches in their Davis Cup world group first round tie on Friday.
Olympic bronze medallist Paes beat Novak 6-2 6-3 6-7 6-3 after Petr Korda had given the fifth-ranked Czechs the lead, beating Mahesh Bhupathi 6-3 6-7 6-1 6-2.
Paes, ranked 105 in the world, constantly attacked, keeping world number 67 Novak off balance with a wide array of deep volleys and drop shots.
Novak held on in the third set to take the tie break 7-5, but Paes broke Novak's opening serve in the fourth set and appeared to have the Czech on the ropes.
Novak fought back only to blow three break points at 1-3, and four at 2-4, before Paes served out the match.
"I got off to a slow start, but really Paes just played very well," said Novak.
Meanwhile Czech number one Korda, ranked more than 450 places higher than his opponent, overcame a spate of unforced errors and a lingering cold to beat Bhupathi.
The veteran Korda, showed few signs of trouble early in the match cruising to the first set in 29 minutes.

But a number of unforced errors allowed Bhupathi to stay in the second set which the Indian player finally won 7-2 in a tie break. Korda, ranked 33rd in the world, eventually shifted his game into high gear to take the next two sets.
"I have had a cold for the past few days and didn't feel 100 percent all of the time...but the main thing is that I got the point because it was expected," he said.
The Czechs are slated to send Martin Damm and Pavel Vizner out on the court for Saturday's doubles against Paes and Bhupathi. The reverse singles are scheduled for Sunday.
